comment: Which upstream settings handler services which chrome.send message, and which
handlers astro://settings installs.
Hand-maintained, and the only hand-maintained input to
tools/tests/cases/settings-sends-reach-an-adopted-handler.sh. The gate joins
three things and is strict in every direction:
* every message the app sends (src/pages/settings/**, via send /
sendWithPromise) is registered by a handler declared below;
* every event the app listens for (addWebUIListener) is fired by one;
* every handler declared below is instantiated by AstroSettingsUI, and
every handler AstroSettingsUI instantiates is declared below.
WHY IT IS WORTH A GATE. chrome.send to a message no installed handler
registered reaches DUMP_WILL_BE_NOTREACHED in
content/browser/webui/web_ui_impl.cc. That is fatal in a DCHECK build and a
SILENT NO-OP in the release build users get: the control draws, the button
depresses, nothing happens, nothing is logged. Four of this page's sections
shipped in that state -- appearance, downloads, on-startup and import --
before the join existed. tsc cannot see it, the dev fixtures answer every
message themselves, and a browser run only finds the buttons someone thought
to press.
`messages` and `events` are the handler's FULL registration, read out of the
file named in `source` at the locked Chromium revision -- not the subset
Astro happens to call. Adopting a handler really does install all of them, so
declaring less would make the gate refuse a call that in fact works.
Regenerate a handler's lists after a Chromium roll by reading its source:
grep -oE 'RegisterMessageCallback\(\s*"[^"]+"' <source>
grep -oE 'FireWebUIListener\(\s*"[^"]+"' <source>
The second misses events pushed through a named constant; the four in this
file that are (profile-info-changed, profile-stats-count-ready and
notification-permission-review-list-maybe-changed) were resolved by hand.

AboutHandler.note: The version, the channel and the update flow. Astro's About section reads it for the update status it pushes on `update-status-changed`.

AppearanceHandler.note: The half of Appearance that is the browser rather than a pref: the Customize side panel and the pinned-toolbar set. `openCustomizeChrome` runs IDC_SHOW_CUSTOMIZE_CHROME_SIDE_PANEL on the last active browser.

BrowserLifetimeHandler.note: Relaunch. The System section's relaunch row is the only caller.

ClearBrowsingDataHandler.note: Browsing-data deletion and the byte counters beside each checkbox. A correctness surface Astro has no reason to own.

DefaultBrowserHandler.note: Whether Astro is the system default, and asking to become it. There is no pref for this on any platform.

DownloadsHandler.note: The download-folder picker, and whether any auto-open file types are set -- the latter has no allowlisted pref, only this handler's `auto-open-downloads-changed`.

ImportDataHandler.note: Importing bookmarks, history, passwords and search engines from another installed browser, plus the HTML-file path.

ManageProfileHandler.note: Renaming the local profile. CHECKs that the trimmed name is non-empty, which is why the You and Astro row disables its button rather than sending an empty string.

ProfileInfoHandler.note: The local profile's name and avatar, and the push that follows a rename.

ResetSettingsHandler.note: Resetting the profile to its defaults, and the list of tampered preference paths the reset banner is built from.

SafetyHubHandler.note: Site permissions automatically revoked for disuse, and the version card. The password and Safe Browsing cards it also serves are Google-service surfaces Astro does not render; registering a message costs nothing until something sends it.

SearchEnginesHandler.note: The search-engine list and which one is default. Astro's own defaults are seeded elsewhere; this is the editor.

SecureDnsHandler.note: The DoH resolver list and the current secure-DNS mode, which is a generated pref pair no settingsPrivate key exposes.

SiteSettingsHandler.note: Per-site permissions. Astro reads only the per-category DEFAULT today; the rest of its surface arrives with the exceptions lists.

StartupPagesHandler.note: The on-startup page list, which is a table model in the browser rather than a pref the page can edit.

SystemHandler.note: One message: hand the user to the desktop environment's own proxy settings. There has never been an in-browser proxy editor on Linux.
